perf: stream cursors instead of fetchall on full-library scans

Five queries read one row per asset and grouped the results in Python, so
`fetchall()` materialized the entire library before any work started. On a
synthetic 200k-row table that is 71 MB of peak allocation; iterating the
cursor instead is ~0, with identical results.

Deliberately not a `--limit` flag. These five are duplicate detection and
habit statistics, where a cap doesn't bound the work, it silently changes the
answer — you miss duplicate pairs, or compute statistics over a sample and
report them as the library total. `--limit` already exists in
cleanup_executor and similarity_finder, where capping what you act on is
meaningful.

The other 52 fetchall() calls are GROUP BY aggregates, PRAGMA introspection,
or already LIMIT-ed, and return tens of rows regardless of library size.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
